Market Research Brief

Verified and structured market research on the global PBX transition to VoIP, covering Taiwan SME digital transformation, regional adoption patterns, security concerns, and regulatory drivers.

1. Taiwan SME Digital Transformation

According to MIC (資策會產業情報研究所), IDC Taiwan, and EVOX market observations: An estimated 60-70% of Taiwan's 1.6 million SMEs still rely on on-premise PBX hardware, with most systems deployed 7-10+ years ago. Major vendors Panasonic, Toshiba, and NEC have exited or reduced PBX investment. Avaya underwent restructuring and pivoted to cloud. Many deployed systems are effectively in EOL/EOS status, maintained by local SI vendors using second-hand spare parts.

2. Key Drivers

  • Hybrid Work & Mobility: Post-pandemic hybrid work requires mobile app extensions and softphones. Legacy EOL PBX cannot integrate these, driving migration to UCaaS.
  • API Integration & Digital Transformation: CRM, Microsoft Teams, LINE, Slack integration requires software-defined communication APIs that legacy PBX/IVR cannot provide.
  • Supply Chain Disruption: EOL means no new hardware, no replacement parts from OEMs. Second-hand spare parts market is unreliable for B2B enterprise products.
  • PSTN Switch-off: BEREC reports EU-wide copper switch-off accelerates. UK BT PSTN shutdown Jan 2027, Germany 2018, Spain 2025. Physical TDM/analog infrastructure loss fundamentally disconnects legacy systems.

3. Regional VoIP Adoption

RegionPaceKey Dynamics
EuropeFast (policy-driven)PSTN switch-off roadmaps from UK, Germany, France, Spain force SIP Trunk/UCaaS migration.
North AmericaFast (market-driven)High SaaS/cloud adoption. On-prem PBX <30% market share. Teams Phone, Zoom Phone, RingCentral dominant.
Asia-PacificPolarizedJapan/Singapore/AU in All-IP era. SE Asia + India still heavily dependent on second-hand TDM/hybrid PBX.
Latin AmericaStable (mobile-first)Long PBX replacement cycles. WhatsApp Business API used as IVR alternative.
AfricaLeapfrog (mobile)Low fixed-line penetration, direct-to-mobile VoIP/cloud communication adoption.

4. Security Concerns

  • EDR/SIEM Blind Spots: EOL PBX runs legacy RTOS/embedded Linux. Cannot install security agents. No syslog over TLS support.
  • Forever-Day Vulnerabilities: No firmware patches for known CVEs (command injection, buffer overflow on web GUI, SIP stack).
  • Plaintext Protocols: SIP on UDP 5060, unencrypted RTP. ARP spoofing enables call interception and DTMF sniffing.
  • IAM Gaps: Static passwords/PIN, no SAML/OIDC, no MFA. ATA shadow IT risk with default credentials.

References: CISA Bad Practices, NIST SP 800-53 (SA-22), OWASP IoT Top 10
